{{Short description|Number n where the highest prime factor of (n^2 + 1) is at least 2n}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Størmer number''' or '''arc-cotangent irreducible number''' is a positive [[integer]] <math>n</math> for which the greatest [[prime factor]] of <math>n^2+1</math> is greater than or equal to <math>2n</math>. They are named after [[Carl Størmer]].

==Sequence==
The first Størmer numbers below 100 are:
{{bi|left=1.6| [[1 (number)|1]], [[2 (number)|2]], [[4 (number)|4]], [[5 (number)|5]], [[6 (number)|6]], [[9 (number)|9]], [[10 (number)|10]], [[11 (number)|11]], [[12 (number)|12]], [[14 (number)|14]], [[15 (number)|15]], [[16 (number)|16]], [[19 (number)|19]], [[20 (number)|20]], 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 39, 40, 42, 44, 45, 48, 49, 51, 52, 53, 54, 56, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 65, 66, 67, 69, 71, 74, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 82, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90, 92, 94, 95, 96, 97... {{OEIS|id=A005528}}. }}

The complementary sequence (numbers below 100 that ''aren't'' Størmer) is only [[3 (number)|3]], [[7 (number)|7]], [[8 (number)|8]], [[13 (number)|13]], [[17 (number)|17]], [[18 (number)|18]], [[21 (number)|21]], [[30 (number)|30]], [[31 (number)|31]], [[32 (number)|32]], [[38 (number)|38]], [[41 (number)|41]], [[43 (number)|43]], [[46 (number)|46]], [[47 (number)|47]], [[50 (number)|50]], [[55 (number)|55]], [[57 (number)|57]], [[68 (number)|68]], [[70 (number)|70]], [[72 (number)|72]], [[73 (number)|73]], [[75 (number)|75]], [[76 (number)|76]], [[83 (number)|83]], [[91 (number)|91]], [[93 (number)|93]], [[98 (number)|98]], [[99 (number)|99]] and [[100]].

==Density==
[[John Todd (computer scientist)|John Todd]] proved that this sequence is neither [[finite set|finite]] nor [[cofinite]].{{r|t}}

{{unsolved|mathematics|What is the natural density of the Størmer numbers?}}
More precisely, the [[natural density]] of the Størmer numbers lies between 0.5324 and 0.905.
It has been conjectured that their natural density is the [[natural logarithm of 2]], approximately 0.693, but this remains unproven.{{r|eh}}
Because the Størmer numbers have positive density, the Størmer numbers form a [[Large set (combinatorics)|large set]].

==Application==
The Størmer numbers arise in connection with the problem of representing the [[Gregory number]]s ([[arctangent]]s of [[rational number]]s) <math>G_{a/b}=\arctan\frac{b}{a}</math>  as sums of Gregory numbers for integers (arctangents of [[unit fraction]]s). The Gregory number <math>G_{a/b}</math> may be decomposed by repeatedly multiplying the [[Gaussian integer]] <math>a+bi</math> by numbers of the form <math>n\pm i</math>, in order to cancel prime factors <math>p</math> from the imaginary part; here <math>n</math> is chosen to be a Størmer number such that <math>n^2+1</math> is divisible by <math>p</math>.{{r|cg}}
